title: A morphism of small groupoids injective on objects is Frobenius exactly when it admits natural finite fibre dual-basis data, equivalently the specified projective and B-linear Hom conditions over local-unit groupoid algebras
author: Juan Jesus Barbaran Sanchez; Laiachi El Kaoutit
source_title: Linear Representations and Frobenius Morphisms of Groupoids
difficulty_reason: The theorem treats arbitrary small groupoids and their rings with enough idempotents, where a global unit and finite-dimensional group algebra cannot be assumed. Its proof must recover fibrewise finite dual bases from a natural equivalence of two adjoints, identify the corresponding unital-module Hom objects, and reconstruct an equivalence on all representations using small projective generators. These compatibility and finiteness obligations go beyond finite-group Frobenius reciprocity or a single induction calculation.

proof_review.note: The complete three-direction proof of Theorem5.3 (Sections5.1–5.3) was read together with the explicit groupoid induction/co-induction constructions and both adjunction proofs in Sections3.3–4.2. The authors extract a natural Frobenius transformation and finite fibre dual-basis data from the adjoint isomorphism, convert that data into finitely generated projective unital local-unit modules and the B-linear Hom identification, and reconstruct the natural adjoint isomorphism using small projective generators. Lemma5.5 provides both maps explicitly and leaves their routine inverse/naturality checks to the reader; its new construction is present. Neither ordinary finite-group reciprocity nor the subgroupoid finite-orbit corollary is selected separately.

statement_scope: Exactly Theorem5.3 over the fixed field k: H and G are small groupoids and phi:H->G is a groupoid morphism whose object map phi_0 is injective. A=kH and B=kG are the associated possibly nonunital algebras with enough orthogonal idempotents; representations and modules use the stated unital local-unit conventions. The equivalence is between the natural isomorphism of the authors induction/right-adjoint and co-induction/left-adjoint functors, the precise natural E transformation with both finite fibre reconstruction identities in (ii), and both the finite-projective AB1_x condition and natural left-B-linear Hom identification in (iii). The finite dual basis is allowed to depend on x. No claim for noninjective object maps, and no separate finite-group or subgroupoid consequence, is selected.
editorial_warning: The terminology induction and co-induction follows this paper: phi^* is the right adjoint and {}^*phi is the left adjoint. The selected statement retains all three equivalent conditions rather than reducing them to an informal equality of induction spaces. Lemma5.5 has explicit forward and inverse formulas with remaining routine verification left to the reader; no omitted new construction is substituted.
